title: Session State doesn't store custom class objects
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I'm trying to prevent streamlit from erasing all my data every time I make an input change. I've used st.forms to handle this and I'm storing data in st.session_state, but it doesn't work for custom objects. 

Namely, I noticed that the memory locations in st.session_state['myObject'] is entirely different depending on where it's accessed (see code below)

(I've tried to post this on streamlit forums but it's giving me an error: 
`An error occurred: Sorry, new users can only mention 2 users in a post.` even though I'm not mentioning any users`) 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
class Dataset:
   def __init__(self)
      self.data = pd.DataFrame(somedata)
   def modify(self)
      self.data = self.data + 1

st.session_state['foo'] = Dataset()

modify = st.button('modify')
save = st.button('save') 

if modify:
   st.session_state['foo'].modify()
   print(st.session_state['foo']) # <class_dataset.Dataset object at 0x17afd6080>

if save:
   st.session_state['foo'].data.to_csv('mydata')
   print(st.session_state['foo']) # <class_dataset.Dataset object at 0x17afab430>
```


### Steps To Reproduce

See code above

### Expected Behavior

Session state version of the object should be the same throughout the two button clicks.

### Current Behavior

Object is different for some reason

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: macOS 13.4.1
- Browser: NA
- Virtual environment: Pipenv
